diagnoses.cost_per_unit: About 7.8 us self per parse call. About 33 us per build_closing_bracket_map call, which is roughly 500 characters at about 65 ns each in a Python while loop. About 7.7 us per _parse_link_href call, a per-character loop over a URL of roughly 30-40 chars. About 1.2 us of dispatch per rendered token.
diagnoses.doubling: All the work is linear in document size: no quadratic paths are visible for this input. Doubling the input roughly doubles wall time, so the gains must come from the constant factor per character and per token.
diagnoses.gap: Several hot helpers still walk strings character by character in Python bytecode where a single compiled-regex or str scan would do. The bracket map scans every character of every paragraph that contains a link. _parse_link_href scans every URL character, and each destination is scanned twice: once
diagnoses.least_work: One C-speed scan over each inline source to find syntax trigger characters, one token per syntax element, and one render call per token. Characters that are not triggers should never be visited by Python bytecode.
diagnoses.unit_count: 18,683 InlineParser.parse calls, 55,819 fast-text scans, 66,171 process_text calls, 4,031 closing-bracket-map builds, 10,762 link-href scans and 91,619 rendered tokens for the 700-section document.
diagnoses.unit_of_work: One inline source string (paragraph, list item, heading, table cell or link text) tokenised by InlineParser.parse and then rendered token by token. Inside it, the inner unit is one source character walked by a Python-level loop.
